title: Closed factorization locus for a constant source
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $Y,X,S$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $i:W\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $f:Y\times_k S\to X$ be a $k$-morphism, with products as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is a unique closed subscheme $L\hookrightarrow S$ such that, for every $k$-scheme $T$ and every $s:T\to S$, the morphism $s$ factors through $L$ if and only if $f\circ(\mathrm{id}_Y\times s):Y\times_kT\to X$ factors through $i$. In particular, this condition represents a subfunctor of $\operatorname{Hom}_k(-,S)$. The same universal property after any base change $S'\to S$ is represented by $L\times_SS'$.

source.place: Theorem 1.105 (printed pp.37–38), together with 1.100–1.101 (printed p.36): pull back the closed subfunctor Mor(Y,W) of Mor(Y,X) along the family S → Mor(Y,X). The test schemes are extended from affine tests by Zariski gluing.

proof.text: Put $D=(Y\times_k S)\times_XW$, with projection $j:D\to Y\times_k S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $j$ is closed. For any $s:T\to S$, the fibre-product property [def-pc-fibre-product] says that $f\circ(\mathrm{id}_Y\times s)$ factors through $i$ exactly when $\mathrm{id}_Y\times s$ lifts to $D$. Closed immersions are monomorphisms by [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed], so all these lifts are unique. Choose a finite affine open cover $Y=\bigcup_a V_a$, $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$; it exists by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $V_a\times_kU$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B_a\otimes_k A)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] identifies it with the open subscheme $\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(V_a)\cap\mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(U)$ of $Y\times_kS$, so it is an affine open there. The restriction of $D$ is affine and, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion], is the spectrum of a quotient $(B_a\otimes_k A)/K_{a,U}$, where $K_{a,U}$ is the kernel of the surjective restriction homomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 1.105, pp.37–38, reduction to affine opens of Y; Example 1.100, p.36; Stacks 01JU (schemes-lemma-fibre-product-immersion), 01I4 (schemes-lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), 01QO (morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Choose a $k$-basis $(e_{a,\lambda})_\lambda$ of each $B_a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free]. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free], the elements $e_{a,\lambda}\otimes1$ form an $A$-basis of $B_a\otimes_k A$, and an $R$-basis of $B_a\otimes_k R$ for every $k$-algebra $R$. Define $J_U\subseteq A$ to be the ideal generated by all coefficients $c_\lambda$ in all finite expansions $z=\sum_\lambda e_{a,\lambda}\otimes c_\lambda$ for $z\in K_{a,U}$ and every $a$. For any $k$-algebra map $\varphi:A\to R$, linear independence over $R$ gives $(1\otimes\varphi)(z)=0$ if and only if every $\varphi(c_\lambda)=0$. Thus $(1\otimes\varphi)(K_{a,U})=0$ for all $a$ if and only if $\varphi(J_U)=0$: annihilating a generated ideal is equivalent to annihilating its generators.

source.place: Lemma 1.102 and Proposition 1.103, pp.36–37: basis-coordinate ideal and equations (6)–(7); Stacks 09FN (fields-lemma-vector-space-is-free).

proof.text: Let $\operatorname{Spec}R\to U$ correspond to $\varphi:A\to R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the chart $V_a\times_k\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B_a\otimes_kR)$, and its map to $V_a\times_kU=\operatorname{Spec}(B_a\otimes_kA)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(1\otimes\varphi)$, since both have the same two projections. On this chart a lift to $D$ is exactly a ring map from $(B_a\otimes_k A)/K_{a,U}$ inducing $1\otimes\varphi$; by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the quotient-ring universal property, this exists exactly when $(1\otimes\varphi)(K_{a,U})=0$. When all these lifts exist they agree on overlaps, since $j$ is a monomorphism by [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed]. They therefore glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to a lift on $Y\times_k\operatorname{Spec}R$. Step 2 proves that the original family factors through $W$ exactly when $\varphi(J_U)=0$, equivalently when $\operatorname{Spec}R\to U$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J_U)$. This includes arbitrary $k$-algebras $R$, with nilpotents and with no finite-type condition. Here [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] identifies the charts $V_a\times_k\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the inverse images of $V_a$ under the first projection; hence they form an open cover.

source.place: Proposition 1.103, p.37, equations (6)–(7), and Theorem 1.105, pp.37–38, gluing over the affine cover of Y; Stacks 00AN (sheaves-lemma-mapping-property-glue).

proof.text: For $h\in A$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](0) identifies $U_h$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A_h$. Both the extended ideal $J_UA_h$ and the independently constructed ideal $J_{U_h}$ have the same annihilating homomorphisms $A_h\to R$: apply Step 3, since the maps $\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ and their induced families are identical whether considered over $U$ or $U_h$. Testing with $R=A_h/(J_UA_h)$ gives $J_{U_h}\subseteq J_UA_h$, and testing with $R=A_h/J_{U_h}$ gives the reverse inclusion. Thus $J_{U_h}=J_UA_h$. This also shows that changing the chosen bases or affine cover cannot change $J_U$, by the same two quotient tests.

source.place: Example 1.100, p.36, uniqueness of the local defining ideals; Stacks 01I3 (schemes-lemma-standard-open-affine) and 01HS (schemes-lemma-standard-open), as stated in the cited node.

proof.text: The ideals $J_U$ are defined for every affine open $U$ of $S$ and satisfy precisely the principal-open compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](1). That node constructs a closed immersion $l:L\hookrightarrow S$ whose restriction over $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J_U)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Consequently Step 3 proves the required factorization equivalence for every affine test whose map to $S$ lands in an affine open of $S$.

source.place: Example 1.100, p.36: glue the local defining ideals; Stacks 01QQ (morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-bijection-ideals) and 01IN (schemes-lemma-closed-subspace-scheme).

proof.text: For an arbitrary $k$-scheme $T$ and $s:T\to S$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], cover each $s^{-1}(U)$ by affine opens $T_b$, with $U$ ranging over affine opens of $S$. Step 5 applies to every $T_b\to U$. If the family on $Y\times_kT$ factors through $W$, its restrictions give lifts $T_b\to L$; these agree on overlaps since $l$ is a monomorphism, and glue to $T\to L$. Conversely, a lift $T\to L$ gives on every $T_b$ a factorization $Y\times_kT_b\to W$. These maps agree on overlaps because $i$ is a monomorphism, and glue to $Y\times_kT\to W$. Use [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] for monicity and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] for both gluings and the equality of the composites. No finiteness or reducedness hypothesis on $T$ is used. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $Y\times_kT_b$ is the inverse image of $T_b$ under the second projection, so these opens cover $Y\times_kT$.

source.place: Theorem 1.105, p.38, local factorization and evaluation; Example 1.100, p.36; affine tests extended to all scheme tests by Stacks 00AN (sheaves-lemma-mapping-property-glue).

proof.text: Factorization through $l$ is unique since $l$ is a monomorphism by [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed]. The map $\operatorname{Hom}_k(T,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}_k(T,S)$ is therefore injective; Step 6 identifies its image with the specified condition. This image is preserved by precomposition, by composition of the factorization through $W$, so it is a subfunctor. If $l':L'\hookrightarrow S$ has the same property, applying it to $T=L,s=l$ and to $T=L',s=l'$ gives maps $L\to L'$ and $L'\to L$ over $S$. Their composites are identities by monicity of $l$ and $l'$, proving uniqueness as a closed subscheme of $S$.

source.place: Example 1.100, p.36, uniqueness of the representing closed subscheme; Proposition 1.101, p.36.

proof.text: For any base change $b:S'\to S$, the projection $L\times_SS'\to S'$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. For every $t:T\to S'$, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies its lifts to $L\times_SS'$ with lifts of $b\circ t$ to $L$. By Step 6 these are exactly the tests for which $f\circ(\mathrm{id}_Y\times(b\circ t))$ factors through $W$. This is the family induced from $f\circ(\mathrm{id}_Y\times b)$ and $t$, since both product morphisms have the same projections. Thus the pullback represents exactly the required base-changed condition, including when $S'$ is not of finite type.

source.place: Proposition 1.101, p.36: pullback of the closed subfunctor; Stacks 01JU (schemes-lemma-fibre-product-immersion).
